subject: logic_tracks.set_automation Write on the MCU rung: whether the one-button warning Logic raises on the Write press is still on screen when the reply returns, and whether quitting Logic afterwards writes a crash report
question: When set_automation asks for Write on the first track, does the base binary's reply return with a one-button Logic dialog still up, does the candidate's reply name the alert it acknowledged and leave no new Logic window, and does the quit after each leave Logic gone without a new crash report?

reverify.expected: the control leaves one one-button dialog up after the reply and 1.5 s later, where none was up before the press; the candidate's reply names informational_alert, acknowledge_alert and modal_after_press clear, a Logic window is listed during the call, none is left after it, and the quit leaves Logic gone with no new Logic Pro crash report; a control quit under the warning in a crash-control language writes one
reverify.cost: needs LPM_LIVE_LOCK naming a held lock and LPM_EVIDENCE_ROOT an absolute path outside the repository; quits and relaunches Logic twice per language and restores Korean at the end, about three minutes per language

method: One run of Scripts/livekit/live_1077_write_warning_is_cleared_in_every_locale.py at ec01c1dbbd216eaa6671602dd27a73183b1082db drove the candidate debug binary (sha256 3d6e863a3563f27df1008fa8e43132a252f34f872fdde8cdd9248cdae64c7f77) and the base binary built from main 9dc6fea2 (sha256 c8502e006ed8283baf313c05f3ad245c0472fd6ce03a17ba5f3880f7b35f3b32), with nothing else holding the MCU ports. For each binary Logic was quit, its AppleLanguages preference set to this language, and the lpm-locale-campaign fixture reopened through live_993_plugin_root_menu_in_every_locale.switch_to, so each Write press was the first of its launch. The host block was generated by Scripts/observation_host.py right after the candidate's launch. The binary then ran logic_navigate toggle_view automation, set_automation read and set_automation write on the first track of logic://tracks. A thread listed Logic's on-screen windows below the pop-up menu level, waiting 20 ms after each listing, from just before the write call until its reply; a window's bounds are those of the listing that first showed it. After the reply, and again 1.5 s later, the window server's list and System Events' count of Logic AXDialog windows with exactly one button were read; each dialog's text is kept as a sha256 and a length. The harness pressed the control's AXDefaultButton after those readings and before the quit. Every quit was read as whether the Logic process was gone and which Logic Pro-*.ips files appeared in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports within 8 s.
conclusion: Base binary: a window at layer 8 appeared during the Write call, first listed 0.793 s into the call and still listed at 4.843 s; the reply came back State B with no modal field, and System Events counted 1 one-button dialog after the reply and 1 again 1.5 s later. The harness then pressed its default button outside the measured bracket, after which System Events counted 0, and the quit left 0 new crash reports. Candidate: a window at layer 8 was listed from 0.803 s to 1.543 s into the call; the reply named informational_alert and acknowledge_alert with modal_after_press clear, and came back State B (readback_unavailable). No window that was not there before the call was listed after the reply or 1.5 s later, System Events counted 0 one-button dialogs at both readings, and the quit left Logic gone with 0 new crash reports.
limits: One track, the first row of logic://tracks, on one fixture and one Logic installation, one Write press per launch. Whether Logic raises the warning on a later press in the same launch, or on another track, was not measured.

The window thread waits 20 ms after each listing. A warning Logic raised and the candidate cleared between two listings would not have been seen; the candidate check requires at least one sighting, so it would have failed rather than passed.

The candidate's sighting is matched to the warning by its layer, position and timing, which are those of the control's window that System Events then counted as the one-button dialog; its text was not read during the call. Bounds are those of the first listing, taken while Logic's opening animation was still small, so whether the candidate's warning finished opening before it was acknowledged is not recorded.

The mode readback is recorded, not judged. The base binary's reply came back State B (readback_unavailable) and the candidate's State B (readback_unavailable), so this run does not show which mode Logic ended in. The first track here is a stack header: its row in logic://tracks reads is_stack_header true.
Which Logic string the dialog carries is not claimed. Its text is a digest and a length, identical across the two binaries' launches only where the digests match.

A crash report is looked for only within 8 s of the quit and only under Logic Pro-*.ips; the crash-reading positive control is the crash-control language's quit, not this language's, where the control's warning was acknowledged first.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record states a fact about the server's BEHAVIOUR -- whether a Logic dialog is still on screen when set_automation replies, read as window numbers, layers and a count of one-button dialogs, and what a quit leaves behind -- not about a string Logic ships. The dialog's text is kept only as a digest.
